reader.requirement: At --std 85 a signed numeric DISPLAY item with SIGN ... SEPARATE [CHARACTER] (written on the item or inherited from a group SIGN clause) stores its sign as an extra leading/trailing character position that is not a digit, counts the S in its size, and uses '+' for positive (including zero) and '-' for negative.

edition-consulted.switches: only the syntax-rule subject screen: at DialectLevel < 2002 GateGroupSignSubordinates refuses a group SIGN clause with no signed subordinate or over a non-DISPLAY subordinate (COBOL0900); the GR6 representation path is not switched
report-group SIGN without SEPARATE refused below 2002; not on the data-item GR6 path

reader.notes: All three lettered items hold across elementary, group-inherited, scaled, ODO, maximum-size and file-record forms at --std 85. The representation path has no edition switch; edition only gates which subjects may carry the clause (syntax rules). Minor: the SR2 refusal message says 'usage is BINARY' for an item the 85 source wrote as COMP.

refuter.evidence: Probe refute-1985-191/r1sep.cob at --std 85 (runs/r1sep-001), aimed at what the reader did not try: negative results that store as zero (COMPUTE A=-0.4 -> [+0]; COMPUTE B=-3*0 -> [00+]; MOVE -0 -> [+000]; COMPUTE D=-1/3 -> [0+]; VALUE -0 -> [+00]); MOVE of a separate-sign item to alphanumeric X(4)/X(3)/X(2) -> [012 ]/[012]/[01] and trailing -> [034 ] (sign character not moved, size one less, as §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4a requires); MOVE to unsigned 99 -> 12; class NUMERIC with the sign position ' ', '*', and an embedded '-' -> NOT, with '+'/'-' -> NUMERIC (§1985:VI.6.3.1.2: valid separate signs are only + and -); INITIALIZE of a group of LEADING/TRAILING SEPARATE items -> [+00000+]; comparison with nonnumeric literal "012" -> EQ; ADD 1 to raw image -099 -> -098. Class c: r1nat.cob refuses USAGE NATIONAL (COBOL0900, 2002 form) and SIGN SEPARATE on PACKED-DECIMAL (COBOL2422); USAGE DISPLAY SIGN IS TRAILING SEPARATE compiles. r3sync.cob: SIGN LEADING SEPARATE SYNC RIGHT item images [-012] and truncates 1234 to [+234]. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.5.12.4 GR6 (the text is in GR6); OK §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4a; OK §1985:VI.6.3.1.2 (lies in GR5). Lead outside this rule: MOVE -100 TO PIC S99 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE stores [+00] at 85 and at 2023 (runs/r1sep-002 at --std 2023), where §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR4b ('the sign of the sending operand is placed in the receiving item', cite OK) read literally gives [-00]; the project's determination (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-85: a negative zero is no distinct value) normalizes it. That is a MOVE-rule question, not GR6's, whose three lettered items all hold.
